findings.suggested_fix: Translate all Bible book names into conventional Modern Hebrew forms and keep the exact chapter:verse numbers unchanged. Use a consistent Hebrew naming convention throughout (examples below). Replace English forms in the HTML while preserving tags and verse numbers. Suggested standard Hebrew forms: 2 Timothy -> "טימותאוס ב'" (or "איגרת טימותאוס השנייה") ; Genesis -> "בראשית" ; 1 Timothy -> "טימותאוס א'" (or "איגרת טימותאוס הראשונה") ; 1 Peter -> "איגרת פטרוס א'" or "פטרוס א'" ; Hebrews -> "איגרת אל העברים" (or "אל העברים") ; Luke -> "לוקס" (או "לוקס"/"לוקס" as used locally) ; Matthew -> "מתי"; Hebrews (chapter 11 ref) -> "אל העברים" ; Note: keep the numeric references exactly as in the source (e.g., "טימותאוס ב' 1:4-7"). Ensure every instance (including parenthetical "see" notes and inline references) is updated. Example replacement in the first paragraph: replace "– 2 Timothy 1:4-7." with "– טימותאוס ב' 1:4–7."

findings.suggested_fix: Standardize transliteration or use the conventional Hebrew Bible/heritage forms for proper names. Suggested forms: Lois -> "לוֹאיס" (or "לואיס" but prefer vocalized "לוֹאיס"); Eunice -> "יוניקה"/"יוניקי"/"אוּניקֶה" (common Hebrew Bibles use "יוניקה" or "יוניקה׳); Anabaptist -> use an accepted Hebrew term such as "אנאבאפטיסטי" or explainatically "קהילות אנאבפטיסטיות". Ensure consistency across the article. Preserve HTML structure when making replacements.
